prize_parts.citation: For the development of general, ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B029 alone, Buchwald and Hartwig. In answer to the chair's question and to Linke, Brzezinski, Aili and Chabes, the conceptual step that separates C-N coupling from the 2010 prize is mechanistic, not only a matter of ligand generations. In C-C coupling the nucleophile arrives as a preformed organometallic that transmetalates. In C-N coupling the nucleophile is a neutral, coordinating amine that has to bind palladium, be deprotonated by a base compatible with the substrate, and then undergo C-N reductive elimination from a palladium amido complex, which is intrinsically slow, while competing beta-hydride elimination from that amido intermediate destroys the product. Solving that required ligands designed against those specific failure modes (chelating bisphosphines first, then bulky electron-rich monophosphines and NHCs), and it opened a different bond class with different scope and process considerations. The proof of generality is practical: aryl amines are among the most frequent bonds made in medicinal and process chemistry, and the method is the default route to them. After about thirty years, independent confirmation is complete and the attribution is clean, with two originators who worked in parallel. Nothing else on the shortlist combines this maturity with a two-name credit that nobody can reasonably contest.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2010 prize remains the main objection, and I accept that a committee which values a new modality over a new bond class will rank B029 below B007. Kosugi's earlier stoichiometric tin-amide chemistry leaves a priority footnote, which the citation wording 'general, ligand-controlled' is meant to address but cannot erase. B029 is also incremental in the sense that the catalytic cycle is the familiar one. If the committee reads novelty as requiring a new mechanism of action in biology or medicine, B029 loses that comparison.

responses.point: Linke asks what conceptual step beyond ligand generations separates C-N coupling from the 2010 precedent, and says he would support it as a strong alternative to B007 if shown.
responses.response: The step is that the nucleophile is not an organometallic. It is a coordinating amine that must be bound and deprotonated at palladium, and the resulting amido complex has a hard reductive elimination and a beta-hydride pathway that C-C coupling does not face. Ligands had to be designed against that failure mode, which is why the first catalysts for C-C coupling did not work for amines. It is a different problem with a different solution, and it created a tool that changed what medicinal chemists can make. I would not claim this is as large a conceptual jump as a new modality, but it is more than an extension.

responses.point: Aili says a second palladium cross-coupling prize is a continuation he would weigh against, and ranks degraders higher on novelty while keeping C-N coupling in reserve.
responses.response: I accept that degraders open a new mode of action, and I have not changed my view on that. My disagreement is on what is new chemically. The ternary-complex cooperativity is a real physical principle, but the molecules are bifunctional ligands made with established medicinal chemistry, and the new part is E3 biology. The three-name attribution is also the weakest point of the B007 case: your slate takes Handa over Deshaies, and the cereblon strand is arguably a separate discovery. I would not give B007 priority on novelty and then discount its attribution. If the committee wants to honour degraders I will not obstruct it, but I would ask the expert report to settle the Handa and Ito question before we vote.

responses.point: Brzezinski keeps B029 in mind as a mature candidacy if B007 is judged premature and asks whether a distinct conceptual step can be shown.
responses.response: I take that as a fair statement of the conditions, and I hope the mechanistic answer above meets the novelty test. B007 is premature in the sense that no degrader is approved and the credit is split across two strands, while B029 has neither problem. On Kosugi, the catalytic, general, ligand-controlled reaction came from Buchwald and Hartwig, and the stoichiometric tin-amide result is background, so the pair stands. I agree with your request that the expert reports be specific about the late-stage degrader trials before we vote.

responses.point: Chabes keeps B029 as his first alternative and would not oppose it as a single-achievement prize instead of his two-part proposal.
responses.response: Thank you. I think a single coherent achievement is the stronger configuration than the two-part B052 plus B007 proposal. On B052 I agree that Liu alone is the right attribution within the cap, but my concern about the 2020 CRISPR prize is about what is chemically new: the conversion is a natural deamination delivered by a programmable protein, so I weigh it as protein engineering and keep it only as an alternative.

responses.point: Zou pairs B029 with B052, agrees on the two-person slate, asks that the citation say general catalytic C-N coupling, and ranks photoredox below B029 on attribution.
responses.response: I agree on the citation wording and have adopted it. I do not support the pairing with B052, since it combines two achievements with no shared theme and the base editing part is the less mature of the two. On photoredox I now agree with you: credit is spread over seven or more names and any three-person cut is open to challenge, so I have dropped B028 from my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the amine-binding, deprotonation and amido-complex reductive elimination problem as a sufficient step beyond the 2010 prize.
Whether the committee values a new modality (B007) over a mature method, which is the real axis of disagreement.
The clinical status of late-stage degraders, which I cannot verify from the files I have.
Whether Kosugi deserves more than a mention in the background.
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate. As the committee's synthetic organic chemist I have a disciplinary lean toward B029 and state it openly; I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr, which is not a tie to any candidate. No recusal.
